title: NaviDiv: A Comprehensive Tool for Monitoring Chemical Diversity in Generative Molecular Design
experiments_summary: The experiments use REINVENT4 with a prior model trained on the FORMED and GEOM3D datasets (organic electronic molecules) to conduct reinforcement learning-based molecular generation for 1000 iterations, producing 100 molecules per step, targeting singlet fission material discovery. The singlet fission scoring function evaluates molecules via a pre-trained Graph Neural Network (Chemprop-based) that predicts S1 and T1 excited-state energies, with additional filters for molecular weight (300–800 Da) and synthetic accessibility score (≤3). Three constraint regimes are compared across 5 independent runs with different random seeds: (1) Baseline with no diversity constraints, (2) Fragment-Based constraints that penalize fragments appearing in more than 5% of molecules in the previous step or in more than 50 total generated molecules (only fragments larger than 8 non-hydrogen atoms), and (3) Combined constraints applying similarity-based penalties (threshold 10%), fragment-based penalties (threshold 5%, fragments >8 non-hydrogen atoms), and n-gram (10-gram SMILES sequence) penalties (threshold 3%). Diversity is assessed throughout training using four complementary metrics: (a) representation distance-based analysis using Morgan fingerprints with Tanimoto similarity and cluster counting, (b) string-based n-gram (10-gram) frequency analysis of SMILES sequences, (c) fragment-based decomposition tracking unique fragment ratios and overrepresented motifs, and (d) scaffold-based analysis. Dimensionality reduction (t-SNE) is applied for chemical space visualization. Performance benchmarking is conducted on an Intel Core i7 CPU with 16GB RAM to measure computational overhead of the diversity analysis pipeline.
